O.outcome_detail: use of pelvic lymph node dissection during LRP

cells.quote: A significant increase was noted in the number of cases in which lymph node dissection was performed as surgical experience increased, with post hoc analysis revealing a significant difference between Group 1 and Group 3 (23.3% vs. 56.7%; p = 0.022).
cells.note: The study is retrospective and chronologically compares cases as the surgeon gained experience; the contrast is not a randomized instructional treatment.

cells.quote: OT decreased progressively with experience, from 251 ± 52 min in Group 1 to 219 ± 40 min in Group 3 (p = 0.027).
cells.note: The study followed one surgeon's consecutive cases rather than randomly assigning learners to conditions.

cells.quote: The mean length of hospital stay decreased from 5.5 ± 1.19 days in Group 1 to 4.1 ± 1.24 days in Group 3 (overall mean: 4.8 ± 1.38 days; p < 0.001).
cells.note: The outcome is a postoperative clinical outcome associated with chronological surgical experience.

cells.quote: The rate of preserved erectile function increased to 50% in Group 3, showing a significant improvement compared with Group 2 (p = 0.012).
cells.note: Erectile function was assessed one year after surgery.

cells.quote: The rates of positive surgical margins were 13.3%, 20.0%, and 3.3% in Groups 1, 2, and 3, respectively (overall 12.2%). Although a numerical decrease was observed in Group 3, the difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.140).
cells.note: The reported decline was statistically non-significant; no equivalence test or adequate-power claim was reported.
